mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that rises by at least 0.4 percentage points from the previous month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE jumps by more than 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more over two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months of >1% INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by at least 0.25% in the same month signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and compresses valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise by >=0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL rise by at least 0.25% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the prior year's average, sustained for three consecutive months, signals a deepening housing market contraction that reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST below prior-year average by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of >10% YoY decline in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month indicates a labor market bifurcation (jobless growth or underemployment), which reduces effective labor productivity and corporate earnings power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent quarterly rise in real GDP (GDPC1) of at least 2.5% over two consecutive quarters signals robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during two consecutive quarters of >2.5% quarterly GDPC1 growth.
